newsitem.title: USA: Michaels sees Q4 at low end of expectations.
newsitem.headline: Michaels sees Q4 at low end of expectations.

text.p: Michael Rouleau, chief executive officer of Michaels Stores Inc, said Wednesday the company's fourth quarter results "will probably be at the lower end of the range of earnings expectations."

Rouleau made the comment as he disclosed that, although the company's year-end physical inventories are not complete, the sell-off of Christmas merchandise and other discontinued items was costly in terms of markdowns.
The First Call mean estimate for Michaels' fourth quarter, fiscal 1997, is $0.36 a share.

At the same time, the company said that lender banks under its revolving credit facility and operating lease facility relating to two distribution sites have extended their waivers of non-compliance through March 15.
The company had previously said that due to a third quarter operating loss, it was not in compliance with a covenant under those facilities.

It said it uses borrowings under the credit facility primarily to finance seasonal working capital requirements and, consistent with its normal seasonal borrowing requirements and current cash position, does not anticipate borrowing under the facility until the second quarter.

It said that due to the third quarter operating loss, it does not expect to return to compliance with its current financial covenants until the second half of 1997. For this reason it said it intends to negotiate further waivers under or amendments to the two facilities.
Under the leasing facility, without a waiver or amendment, lease obligations of about $28 million could be accelerated, in which case it anticipates refinancing the two distribution sites, it said.

It said it believes it will have enough cash generated from operations, which together with further waivers, amendments or replacements to the credit and leasing facilities will meet its liquidity requirements for next year.
